items.title: Is it right to ask the patient? Nurses' experiences with recruiting patients for research projects in palliative care: a reflexive thematic analysis
items.summary: Background: Several challenges have been identified in recruitment in palliative care research. Previous research has largely focused on barriers and facilitators on recruitment. Aims: To explore nurses’ experiences with recruiting patients when established barriers and facilitators were considered.

items.title: Mapping research trends in preferences for place of death in nursing: a bibliometric analysis
items.summary: Background Preferences for place of death are increasingly recognised as an important component of end-of-life care and patient-centred practice. Aims This study aimed to examine global research trends on preferences for place of death in the nursing-related literature using bibliometric methods.

items.title: Staffs hospices join forces on pioneering home care initiative
items.summary: Four hospices in Staffordshire are working on a joint initiative to bring specialist palliative and end-of-life care into people’s homes, via what is thought to be one of the first collaborations of its kind.

items.title: The future of palliative and end-of-life care
Minister McGovern speech at the Hospice UK conference
District nurse ‘cuts’ to blame for rising end of life A&E visits, says RCN
items.summary: A decline in district and community nursing roles has led to a rise in people at the end of life having to turn to A&E departments for help, the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has warned. RCN general secretary and chief executive Professor Nicola Ranger said there were now ‘too few’ nurses in the community...

items.title: Scotland’s hospices receive funding to match NHS pay rates
items.summary: Hospices in Scotland are being given government funding to provide their staff with pay parity in line with their NHS counterparts.
